title.narrative: Trade Mark East Africa Core Support

description.narrative: Program for Regional Economic Integration in East Africa focusing on lowering trade and transport costs through trade facilitation (and infrastructure) and capacity building. Program targets public sector, private sector and civil society.

Program for regional ekonomisk integration i Östafrika med fokus på att sänka handels och transportkostnader genom handelsprocedurförenklingar och kapacitetsbyggnad. Målgruppen är offentliga liksom private sektorn och civila samhället.

TradeMark East Africa (TMEA) is a DFID-created not-for-profit company that aims to strengthen regional integration and improve trade competitiveness in East Africa. It was set up in 2009 with offices in each of the East African Community (EAC) member states (Burundi, Kenya, Rwanda, South Sudan, Uganda, and Tanzania). From 2011 - 2017 it implemented Strategy 1, focusing on promoting trade along major transport corridors in East Africa. The overarching goal of TMEA is to contribute to increased growth and reduced poverty in East Africa. The purpose of the contribution, thus the impact objective is to support greater regional integration and trade competitiveness in East Africa. In order to reach this impact objective there are four separate outcome objectives: -Reduction in transport and related costs along the key corridors in East Africa (35%)-EAC Institutions develop a comprehensive framework for regional Integration (20%)-Partner states substantially increase the implementation of a comprehensive framework for regional integration (30%)-Private sector and civil society positively influence regional integration policies and practices for growth in trade (15%)

The overall intended outcomes included: reduced transport time and increased volumes; increased ease of trading across borders; enhanced business environment for trade; improved export capability; and efficient trade logistics services. Progress was strong, and included: - Clearance at the first point of entry took place for 100% of Partner States’ selected goods, under the single customs territory. - There was a substantial reduction in overall customs clearance time, - 86 policies relating to the business environment for trade were adopted with support from TMEA. - Each country improved its scores for “logistics competence and quality of service” indicators (measured as part of the World Bank’s logistics performance index)
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
